column3: “Enforces the battle lines.” The main frontline. Enforcers mark where each team should stand in a fight and are the ones who start it, creating space for the rest of their team to capitalize.
“Duels opponents.” A duelist's main job is to pick a target and kill it, either supported by their team or alone. Duelists excel at 1v1 fights.

“Controls the enemy's options.” Through debuffs, taxing, crowd control, area damage or any other means, a controller dictates what the opponent can and can't do, sometimes while supporting their own team.

“Fixes the match in their favour.” Fixers come in many shapes and sizes. Some are not proficient in combat but carry an arsenal of supporting utility; others increase board presence. Either way, they add serious value to a win.
Focused on protecting themselves or their teammates. Wants to survive a long time. Not the best at pushing the frontline forward, but great at holding it.
Deals a lot of damage while having a lot of health. Somewhat individualistic. Advances the frontline by killing the enemy frontline.
Wants to get behind the enemy frontline and crunch it together with their team. High movement and some survivability.
Plays mainly in the frontline, supporting the Enforcers by pressuring the enemy frontline. Can both create scraps (put enemies low) and take scraps (finish off low enemies).
Plays further away from the team: VERY long range, VERY close range, or somewhere in between. Wants to take scraps, or even one-shot enemies.
Can play with the pack, alone, or alongside an ally. Very high movement and escapability. Wants to create scraps.
Controls by denying the enemy team's options: denying space (usually with structures) or stunning.
Controls by weakening the enemy team, with plenty of debuffs or board manipulation tools.
Controls by punishing the enemy team. Great at area damage and crowd control.
Creates an advantage by having more entities on the board than the opponents: creating them and giving the team more options.
Brings loads of utility, mainly to help the team rather than debuff the opponents: buffs, movement options or action economy.
Main goal is to keep allies alive: healing them, preventing damage or helping them escape, so the team stays in the fight.
